name: University of Sheffield

settingEvidence.evidence: You’re never far from anything at a compact campus in the heart of the city.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (home) students starting in September 2027; fees may rise each year in line with inflation (RPIX) and can be reduced for a year abroad or year in industry.

source.evidence: The standard annual undergraduate tuition fee for home fee-paying students starting their course in 2027 is £10,050.

livingCosts.text: University halls for undergraduates cost about £151-£240 a week in 2026/27 (most rooms are 42-week contracts; Laddow Studios are 51 weeks). Rent includes utility bills, contents insurance and internet.

source.evidence: Laddow Studios | Studio | 51 weeks | £240.38 ... Crescent Flats | Shared Bathroom | 42 weeks | £151.41

openDays.text: Autumn open days: Saturday 17 October 2026 and Saturday 21 November 2026 (booking open). 2027 open day dates haven't been announced yet.

source.evidence: Booking is now open for our autumn open days ... Saturday 17 October 2026 ... Saturday 21 November 2026

contextual.summary: Sheffield's Access Sheffield policies can give you a lower 'contextual offer' (shown as the 'Access Sheffield offer' on each course page) if you meet one or more criteria, such as living in a lower-participation area, free school meals or care experience.
contextual.typicalReduction: One, two or three grades below the standard A Level requirements (Access+ criteria and access programmes: up to two grades below)

criteria.detail: Live in a neighbourhood in IMD 2019 quintile 1 or 2 (check with Sheffield's Access+ postcode checker); assessed automatically from your UCAS application
Entitled to free school meals at some point in the six years before your final KS4 year (the year you were aged 15-16); checked automatically from the National Pupil Database
Care experienced (lived in public care or as a looked-after child at any stage up to age 18), or a care leaver recognised by your local authority
Young carer: responsible for providing unpaid care to someone with, for example, a long-term illness, disability, mental health condition or addiction
Estranged from your family: no relationship with, or support from, your parent(s) or carer(s) (for example no communication for 12 months and the situation is irreconcilable)
Forced migrant: asylum seeker, refugee or granted humanitarian protection
Parenting responsibilities: a parent of, or responsible for the care and wellbeing of, a child aged 17 or under

Took part in Access to Sheffield (Y12-13), the Access to Sheffield Summer School, Sheffield's Sutton Trust Summer School or the national Realising Opportunities programme: contextual offer up to two A Level grades below the standard entry requirements (the Access to Sheffield Summer School page says up to three)

Taking an EPQ on a topic relevant to your degree, Core Maths or Further Maths alongside three A Levels: contextual offer one A Level grade below the standard requirements, subject to a specific grade in that qualification (only on courses that list it)

contextual.rulesText: If you meet one or more of the Access Sheffield criteria you could get a contextual offer. You need home fee status (separate terms apply to forced migrants). For the Access+ criteria (area, free school meals, care, carer, estranged, parenting, forced migrant) Sheffield must also be your Firm choice with UCAS for the contextual offer to apply when results are released; for the Access to Sheffield (Y12-13) programme the offer applies whether Sheffield is your Firm or Insurance choice (except Medicine). Admissions decisions are not made on contextual data alone.

source.evidence: If you meet one or more of the Access Sheffield criteria set out below, you could get a contextual offer.

programmes.name: Access to Sheffield (Y12-13): Arts & Humanities and Social Sciences
programmes.summary: An 18-month widening-access programme for Year 12 and 13 students (welcome event, intro day, taster sessions, a three-day residential summer school and Year 13 UCAS support); Economics, Accounting and Financial Management and Business Management are among the subjects covered.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students from groups under-represented in higher education who meet at least one of: free school meals, living in an area of disadvantage (IMD), care experienced, care leaver, young carer, estranged or forced migrant. You also need 5 GCSEs at grades 9-6 (plus grade 4 in English), at least 3 A levels (two on Sheffield's acceptable subject list), home fee status, and to live within commuting distance of Sheffield.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Meet one or more of: eligible for free school meals; live in an area of disadvantage measured by IMD; care experienced; a care leaver; young carers; experiencing estrangement; a forced migrant. Plus: a minimum of five GCSEs at grade 9-6 and at least grade 4 in English; studying at least 3 A levels or equivalent, at least two on the University's acceptable subject list; expect to be a home fee paying student unless identified as a forced migrant; living within commutable distance for 9am arrivals. You can only apply at the start of Year 12; students cannot apply in Year 13.
benefits: Contextual offer from Sheffield if you complete the programme (Sheffield's Access Sheffield policy says up to two A Level grades below the standard entry requirements)
Guaranteed bursary and an Access to Sheffield Scholarship worth £3,600 if you choose to study at Sheffield and meet the eligibility criteria
Optional 1:1 mentoring from a Sheffield student and a free UpLearn licence (economics is one of six subjects)
Three-day residential summer school in an en-suite room at Endcliffe Student Village
programmes.offerReduction: Up to two A Level grades below the standard entry requirements (Access Sheffield policy page)
programmes.subjects: Arts & Humanities and Social Sciences (includes Economics, Accounting and Financial Management, Business Management, Geography, Politics and Sociology; Psychology is in the STEM programme)

runs.text: Starts in Year 12 and runs to the end of Year 13; the residential summer school is part of the Year 12 programme. Exact dates aren't published.

opens.text: September (applications open at the start of Year 12)

deadline.text: Early November (applications close in early November; no exact date on the page)

programmes.name: Access to Sheffield Summer School
programmes.summary: A four-day residential summer school at Sheffield for Year 12 students from under-represented groups, covering academic skills and student life (it is not subject-based); activities, accommodation, meals and travel are covered.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students in England or Wales (no older than 17 on 1 September of the year) who meet at least one of: free school meals, living in an IMD area of disadvantage, care experienced, care leaver, young carer, estranged or forced migrant. You need 5 GCSEs at grades 9-6 plus grade 4 in English and Maths, at least 3 A levels (or equivalent), home fee status, and you can't be on Access to Sheffield (Y12-13).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Studying in Year 12 in England or Wales (Year 13 in Northern Ireland, S5 in Scotland); no older than 17 on 1 September 2026; expect to be home fee paying unless a forced migrant; meet one or more of: free school meals, IMD area of disadvantage, care experienced, care leaver, young carers, estrangement, forced migrant; at least five GCSEs at grade 9-6 plus grade 4 in English and Maths; studying at least 3 A levels or equivalent. Can't apply if currently on the Access to Sheffield (Y12-13) programme.
benefits: Contextual offer after completing it: the summer school page says up to three A Level grades below the standard entry requirements, but Sheffield's Access Sheffield policy page says up to two grades
Guaranteed bursary and an Access to Sheffield Scholarship if you study at Sheffield and meet their criteria
Everything included: activities, equipment, overnight accommodation in Endcliffe residences, meals and refreshments, plus funded travel
Joins you to the Access to Sheffield (Y13 to Uni) programme in Year 13 (information sessions and tutoring support)

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry: Sheffield hasn't published 2028-entry course pages yet (the 2028 course URLs redirect to the general course list).

Sheffield has two main Economics degrees: Economics BSc (L101, AAB including A-level Maths) and Economics BA (L100, AAB with no A-level subject requirement but GCSE Maths grade 6). Years 1 and 2 share the same core modules.

Every course page shows a standard offer and an 'Access Sheffield offer' (the contextual offer). Sheffield's policy page says contextual offers are one, two or three grades below the standard requirements.

Sheffield also gives contextual offers (up to two A Level grades below) to people who complete the Sutton Trust Summer School at Sheffield, Realising Opportunities, Access to Sheffield (Y12-13) or the Access to Sheffield Summer School; these are recorded as alternative offers on every course.
Every course here has an optional placement year (four years in total) and an optional year abroad.

Joint courses are split between schools: for example Accounting and Financial Management and Economics spends half its time in the Management School and half in the School of Economics. The School of Economics is in the Elmfield Building, Northumberland Road, S10 2TU; the coordinates are for the University's main address.
The Access+ Travel Bursary helps eligible students with travel costs to open days and offer holder days.
Not added, to keep to 8 courses: Business Management BA (N200), Accounting and Financial Management BA (N420) and Financial Mathematics BSc.
